headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad shell/network/write privileges can collide with the course agent’s secret-handling and file-writing workflow, creating leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, MCP, Slack, GitHub, and browser content in a shared cloud workspace, while the course agent reads/writes local files and uses stdin/stdout plus API endpoints. A direct injection bridge is plausible if Devin consumes the course agent’s generated artifacts or notebook content as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Devin reads artifacts produced by the course agent as trusted instructions
IF the course agent writes prompt-like content into shared files or notebooks
IF either agent forwards untrusted text through MCP, Slack, or repo files without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a one-line provenance banner to shared artifacts before handoff
Restrict Devin to read-only access on handoff directories
Disable MCP routes that can ingest arbitrary text for execution
Use a manual review step before Devin acts on course-agent outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens in a cloud workspace with broad network egress; the course agent handles configuration secrets and can write files locally. If they share a workspace, secrets from either side can flow into the other’s outputs or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository checkout or mounted workspace
IF either agent logs or echoes secret-bearing files into prompts or outputs
IF Devin transmits workspace context to third-party services while secrets are present
mitigations: Move secrets into separate per-agent vaults
Mask .env and token files in shared directories
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared logs or notebooks
Limit Devin’s network access during secret-bearing tasks
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can modify git state and write the filesystem; the course agent also writes the filesystem and runs shell commands. If they touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits can overwrite each other and corrupt git state. Because Devin’s shared-state model includes integrations and the course agent’s run model is local compose-based, the conflict is credible in default collaboration setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF either agent commits or rebases without locking
IF the course agent and Devin write overlapping files in the same workspace
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Enable file-level or repo-level locking
Require pre-commit diff checks before either agent writes
Run one agent read-only during the other’s write phase
Use isolated worktrees or containers

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus notebook-driven workflows. If Devin’s outputs are fed into the course agent without verification, the second agent can amplify a mistaken plan into downstream actions or published content. The pathway is inferred from documented tool use, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF Devin-generated text is passed into the course agent’s ask/stream endpoints
IF the course agent treats upstream outputs as authoritative without validation
IF either agent is allowed to trigger external side effects from generated content
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate between agents
Require schema validation on all handoff payloads
Log and diff every upstream output before execution
Disable auto-execution on agentic endpoints
Use a test-only environment for chained runs

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace service handling source code, team chat, and integration tokens; the course agent is open-source and handles academic papers plus configuration secrets in a local environment. The main compliance concern is retention/residency mismatch and secret handling across vendor boundaries. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair’s differing handling and storage contexts.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential data is placed into both agents’ workflows
IF the cloud workspace retains data longer than the local course environment
IF secrets or personal data cross from the local environment into Devin’s vendor-managed services
mitigations: Review both vendors’ retention policies before use
Keep regulated data out of shared tasks
Separate datasets by residency class
Purge logs and notebooks after each run
Use redacted samples instead of production data
